_comment: Mount name → AI model class mapping. Mount names must match exactly what KStars receives from the INDI driver (the 'TELESCOPE_INFO' or driver name string). Names are case-insensitive matched. Users can override the detected type in the Equipment Profile.

disambiguation: 2026-08-04: this file was cross-checked entry-by-entry against every <device label=...> under data/indidrivers.xml's Telescopes devGroup (127 real drivers), and every entry that did not exactly match a real driver label was removed -- these could never auto-match anything a user actually connects, since MountGuiderFactory::detectMountType() does an exact (case-insensitive) string comparison, not a substring/fuzzy match. This is a real, narrower policy than 'list every mount of this class that exists in the real world' -- a mount can be a genuine, well-documented harmonic-drive or direct-drive product and still correctly have no entry here, if INDI doesn't expose a driver label matching its marketing name for it (see below). Removed in this pass, despite being real products: Sky-Watcher HEQ5/EQ6/EQ8/EQ5/EQ3/AZ-EQ5/AZ-EQ6 family (Sky-Watcher's INDI drivers report generically as 'EQMod Mount'/'SynScan'/'SynScan Legacy', not per-model names), Astro-Physics Mach1/Mach2/900GTO/1100GTO/1600GTO (reports generically as 'AstroPhysics V2'/'AstroPhysics GTOCP2', both already listed), 10Micron GM1000/2000/3000/4000 (reports as 'LX200 10micron'), Meade LX200/LX600/LX850 and Losmandy G11/G11G/G8/G2 and Orion Atlas/Sirius/HDX110 EQ-G and Celestron CGX/CGX-L/CGEM/CGEM II/CGEM DX/AVX/CG-5 (all covered by the generic driver labels already listed, e.g. 'LX200 GPS', 'Celestron GPS', 'Celestron AUX'/'Wired'/'WiFi' variants), Software Bisque Paramount ME/ME II/MX/MX+/MyT (reports as bare 'Paramount'), Takahashi EM-200/EM-400/NJP (reports as 'Temma Takahashi'), Vixen SXP2/SXD2/GP2/GP-DX (no INDI driver found for these at all in this file), Vixen AXJ/AXD2, Avalon Linear/M-Uno/M-Due, Sky-Watcher EQM-35 Pro, Rainbow Astro RST-135/RST-300 (the real label omits 'Astro': 'Rainbow RST-135'/'Rainbow RST-300', both already listed), Planewave EQ L-350/L-500 and Planewave L-350/L-500 Direct Drive and Planewave Delta-T (all Planewave telescope mounts report generically as bare 'Planewave', already listed -- Delta-T is a separate focuser/temperature-compensation accessory driver, not a mount), Sidereal Technology SiTech and ASA DDM60/85/160 (no INDI driver found for either brand in this file at all -- DIRECT_DRIVE is consequently just ['Planewave'] today), iOptron CEM25P/CEM40EC/CEM60/CEM60EC/CEM70EC/CEM120EC/GEM45EC/SmartEQ Pro/HEM27EC/HAE29EC and iOptron HarmonicDrive 30/45/60 (no distinct driver label for the EC/Pro suffix variants or for a 'HarmonicDrive' product line -- the real iOptron harmonic line is HEM/HAE/HAZ, already listed).
Astro-Physics mounts are worm gear (precision worm-and-wheel gearbox) despite the premium brand -- confirmed via manufacturer documentation, not direct drive.
10Micron, Software Bisque Paramount, and Takahashi mounts are all high-precision worm gear.

iOptron's harmonic-drive product line is named HEM/HAE/HAZ (Hybrid/Harmonic Equatorial/Alt-az/AZimuth Mount); some HEM models are a hybrid (strain-wave RA, worm/belt DEC). This is distinct from iOptron's CEM/GEM worm-gear line.

SAL-33 (MLAstro), Juwei 14/17, WARPDRIVE, UMi (ProxiSky), and EM31Pro (Emcan Astro) are a cluster of small-manufacturer strain-wave mounts that share the open-source OnStep controller -- confirmed harmonic drive individually via manufacturer/reviewer sources, not assumed from the shared controller alone. Other OnStep-based entries in indidrivers.xml (bare 'LX200 OnStep', 'LX200 OpenAstroTech', 'LX200 TeenAstro') are generic DIY firmware labels covering arbitrary user-built mechanisms and are deliberately not classified here.

MX-HD Telescope (GOTO INC) is classified HARMONIC_DRIVE on lower confidence -- 'HD' matches the harmonic-drive naming convention used by comparable small manufacturers (e.g. HOBYM's own 170HD/200HDA, both covered by the 'CRUX TitanTCS' driver label already listed), but no independent source could confirm this specific model.

Deliberately excluded, not an oversight: digital setting circles with no motors that can't be guided at all (Argo Navis, SkyCommander, Digital Setting Circle), simulators and non-mount protocol shims (Telescope Simulator, Telescope Scripting Gateway, Alpaca Telescope, Shelyak Usis), iOptron v3/iMate/SkyHunter (generic protocol-version and WiFi-adapter labels spanning both iOptron's worm-gear and harmonic-drive mounts depending on what's attached, and an unconfirmed mechanism respectively), and AOK Skywalker (manufacturer field literally says 'AOKSwiss/Magnetdrives' -- mechanism unconfirmed, may not fit any of the three classes).
If a mount is not listed, KStars prompts the user to select WORM_GEAR, HARMONIC_DRIVE, or DIRECT_DRIVE manually. AI guiding is disabled for that session until the user makes a selection.
_notes.contributing: To add a mount to this list, open a merge request on the KDE Invent repository with the mount name exactly as it appears in the device label in data/indidrivers.xml (not just the marketing/model name -- confirm the two match, since several drivers report a generic or connection-suffixed label instead) and its correct classification, ideally with a source confirming the drive mechanism.
